study type: Qualitative study using semi-structured interviews and focus group discussions
outcome: Obstetric caregivers' rationales for caesarean section (CS) use
Factors contributing to potential CS overuse
cohort: Obstetric caregivers (consultants, specialists, residents, and midwives) at a university hospital in Tanzania
finding: Obstetric caregivers attributed the high CS rate to various factors outside their control, including economic incentives, maternal demand, fear of blame, and lack of support from senior colleagues, highlighting the complex interplay of factors influencing CS decision-making.
